speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) among the recent spate of home fires, whether there are increasing cases of electrical related fires; and (b) what further preventive measures can be put in place to tackle fires related to electrical appliances and devices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF), in partnership with the People's Association, the National Fire and Emergency Preparedness Council (NFEC) and the Community Emergency and Engagement Committees, has been organising a series of Community Resilience Days in the heartlands to raise the level of fire safety awareness among residents.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SCDF has also been working with the NFEC and HDB to educate new homeowners on fire safety and emergency preparedness through the MyNiceHome Roadshows.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: After a residential fire, SCDF will conduct door-to-door engagements with the residents of the affected block to share fire safety tips.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This includes distributing brochures which advises on preventing battery and personal mobility device (PMD) fires.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SCDF regularly reviews the Fire Code, which stipulates the fire safety requirements for buildings in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For residential premises built before June 2018 and therefore not mandated to install HFADs, homeowners are encouraged to install them nevertheless.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SCDF will continue to work with partners to increase public awareness of fire prevention and how residents may stay safe in the event of a fire at home.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I do encounter a few of these fires in my constituency and quite a number were electrical related.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, perhaps, the Minister of State can share a little bit more about some of the numbers that he mentioned, specifically, details of the causes of the fires for those incidents.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: We know every household fire, besides the casualty, was devastating to families, to neighbours and also to firefighters and first responders.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And also, how can we make our homes and neighbourhood more fire safe?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I will share more details about the numbers, year by year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, for the number of electrical fires, it has remained stable over the years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Indeed, we agree with the Member that even though we saw the numbers decreasing, every fire would cause disruptions to lives and some lives have been lost.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We continue to work together with the community, as well as from the professional angle, we want to make sure that we continue to review and put in place fire safety standards.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the same time, our SCDF officers will do their best to go and respond as fast as they can and put out the fire.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will also continue to enhance and raise awareness on fire safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I hope that we can get more and more people to be on board to be part of this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But above all, I think it is the personal responsibility.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: How we, the Members of the House including myself, as well as well fellow Singaporeans, can play our part: one, to not be complacent about fire safety; and second, how we can make our home safe in terms of our daily activities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Today, we travel a fair bit and we are able to do many online shopping.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Some of these devices that we use in Singapore, we also must take upon our ownership to see whether they are suitable for use here, and also, how we can make sure that if left unattended, that they do not give rise to fire risk.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, while the community, organisations and agencies continue to enhance fire safety standards and raise awareness, I hope this is something that we have come together for.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We can see some of the reports that we have seen about fires.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, even though numbers have been going down, I think it is important for us to bring the message home and each of us has a role to play in this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to get more and more people to be aware, to be conscious and put our concern into actions so that we can keep the fire risk as low as possible.
